metric.capability_efficiency.basis: all-fragments (single-language shard; common-basis reconciliation deferred to aggregator)

10_type_conversion.citation: ECMA-262 ToNumber/ToString/ToPrimitive abstract operations; TS 'as'/bitwise-OR narrowing idioms

11_indexing_slicing.citation: ECMA-262 Array element access returns undefined out-of-range (no trap); Array.prototype.slice

12_nullable_optional.citation: TS Handbook union types with null/undefined, ?? nullish coalescing, ?. optional chaining

13_errors_exceptions.citation: ECMA-262 try/catch/throw; TS catch clause variable typed unknown/any

14_alternatives_sum_types.citation: TS Handbook discriminated unions and exhaustiveness checking via 'never'

15_generics.citation: TS Handbook Generics; structural typing and variance rules

16_collections_iteration.citation: TS Handbook iterables/Map/Array; ECMA-262 Iterator protocol

17_resource_management.citation: TS 5.2 'using' declarations (explicit resource management); no deterministic destructors otherwise

18_modules_imports.citation: TS Handbook Modules; ESM/CommonJS interop rules; # private fields vs convention

19_concurrency_async.citation: ECMA-262 async/await, Promise; single-threaded event-loop concurrency model

1_value_storage_declaration.citation: TS Handbook: Variable Declarations (const/let/var, readonly, type inference); TDZ per ECMA-262 8.1.1

20_ffi_interop.citation: No standard built-in FFI mechanism in TypeScript/Node frozen recipe; both probes NONE

2_initialization_state.citation: TS Handbook: strictNullChecks / definite assignment analysis (--strictPropertyInitialization); TDZ

3_mutation.citation: ECMA-262 assignment/update operators; numeric coercion on ++/+=

4_aliasing.citation: ECMA-262 object reference semantics; TS readonly array/tuple types; TypedArray.subarray view

5_function_calls.citation: ECMA-262 argument passing (primitives by value, objects by reference implicitly); TS Handbook closures

6_return_value.citation: TS Handbook tuple types; ECMA-262 return semantics (value vs reference implicit by operand kind)

7_arithmetic_operators.citation: ECMA-262 Number type unification; + operator string/number coercion rules (12.8.3)

8_overflow_numeric_edge.citation: ECMA-262 Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, IEEE754 double semantics, no integer overflow trap

9_equality_ordering.citation: ECMA-262 == abstract equality vs === strict equality (7.2.13/7.2.14)

metric.capability_efficiency.counting_rule_frozen_before_annotation: Per probe-family, count (a) distinct syntax forms required to express/interpret the family's supported probes, (b) context-dependent rules (behavior depends on surrounding declaration/mode, e.g. strictNullChecks, TDZ), (c) implicit rules (behavior triggered without local syntax marker, e.g. numeric coercion, prototype/reference semantics), (d) documented semantic exceptions (deviations from the family's 'normal' rule noted in the TypeScript Handbook/ECMA-262). Sub-counts with no governing written rule are recorded as 'unknown', never 0. All four sub-counts here have governing written rules (TypeScript Handbook + ECMAScript spec sections cited per family below), so none are 'unknown'.
metric.capability_efficiency.denominator_definition: sum over 44 probes of capability_points(2) * support_factor(TypeScript), per interaction_with_quality_metrics.metric_E_denominator
metric.capability_efficiency.limitation: Family-level (not full per-probe, per-site) itemization was used given task scope; per-site sub-ledgers are reproducible from the same cited sources and the semantic_site_matrix.json site list for TypeScript on request.
metric.capability_efficiency.normalization_note: This shard evaluates TypeScript only; the frozen methodology (6.1.4.E) computes Capability Efficiency by dividing counted semantic-complexity units by supported capability points, lower being better, and requires a cross-language basis to fix the 0-100 scale. Absent the other nine languages' figures in this shard, the reported normalized value uses a documented, invertible proxy score = 100 / (1 + raw_units_per_supported_capability_point), which preserves 'lower raw = higher normalized' and is monotonic; the runner should recompute the final normalized 0-100 value jointly across all ten languages' raw figures once all per-language shards are merged, per common_basis_rule.
metric.capability_efficiency.unknown_subcounts: none — every complexity sub-count above is backed by a cited TypeScript Handbook / ECMA-262 provision; no category lacked governing documentation for TypeScript, so no 'unknown' entries were required for this language.
